messages:
sara: FYI I'm seeing sustained memory growth from KV cache for long-lived sessions on dedicated-prod-3. Dumped stats and a short profile.
mike: Ugh, guess it's that long-context customer again. Do you have numbers?

sara: quick snapshot from 2h ago (trimmed):
```
$ kv-cache-stats --model redwood-7b --node dedicated-prod-3 --window 2h
entries: 1,187,412
mem_used: 21.9GB
avg_entry: 18.9B
fragmentation: 13.7%
page_evictions: 8,432 (LRU threshold=60s)
long_context_sessions (>30k tokens): 98 active
```
Fragmentation + stable entry growth looks suspicious, not just churn.

jia: What eviction policy are we using there? LRU per-shard? Any sticky session keys keeping prefixes pinned?

sara: It's sharded LRU with a per-shard soft cap. We pin session prefixes for "session_sticky=true" keys. Suspect two things: 1) sticky sessions with very long prefixes never get evicted because they keep being referenced; 2) partial prefix reuse creates small hot entries that fragment physical pages.

henry: Can you repro locally with a synthetic workload? I can run a stress job that opens 200 sessions and streams 50k tokens in each.

sara: I ran a quick local replay of customer traces with our kv-pager enabled: we see amortized write amplification when entries are fragmented across pages. Paging logic currently treats entries as append-only segments; updates create new fragments and old ones are tombstoned until compaction.

mike: Do we have compaction running online? We used to, but turned it off for throughput.

sara: Compaction is scheduled but only triggers when free_pages < 5% per-shard. With long contexts we never cross that threshold because mem_used grows and we avoid freeing pages often.

perf-bot: perf/regression-alert: kernel v2.3.1 changed page_alloc path -> +6% median kv-alloc latency on P100 nodes (rolled back in canary)

mike: That kernel bump aligns with the start of these customer reports. Did deploy-bot roll a rollback?

deploy-bot: rollback applied for kernel v2.3.0 -> v2.2.9 on dedicated-prod-3 at 1773499200

jia: Two-prong mitigation plan: 1) tune eviction for sticky-prefixes (TTL or max_prefix_entries); 2) add opportunistic compaction for fragmented pages under high fragmentation ratio.

henry: For (1) I'd propose a cache key change: split session_key into session_id + prefix_signature and make prefix_signature hash-qualified to expire after N tokens or time. That lets us keep session stickiness for routing but avoid unbounded prefix retention.

mike: (+1) Maybe also store a small usage_count per-prefix to let cold prefixes be aged faster. Implementation: increment on reuse, otherwise decay. That avoids sharp evictions on bursts.

sara: Did a quick experiment: replayed one customer trace with TTL=30m for prefix_signature + opportunistic compaction every 5k updates. Results: peak mem down ~18%, fragmentation -> 5%, average token latency unchanged.

sara: sample output: 
```
before: mem=22.1GB frag=14.2% evictions=8432
after : mem=18.1GB frag=5.1% evictions=912 (more but smaller)
latency p50 tokens: 12ms -> 12.6ms (noise)
```

jia: Good signal. Can you add the experiment to a perf job and run for 24h across 3 nodes? Need to ensure compaction doesn't regress p99.

sara: Will schedule. Henry, can you sketch the key-change RFC? Keep the API surface identical for users (session_id still works) but change internal cache keying.

henry: I'll draft RFC: internals only, keys = sha256(session_id) + rolling-prefix-hash(token_window). Rolling-prefix-hash rotates every 1k tokens or 30m.

mike: Also add metric: kv.prefix_ages.histogram and kv.fragmentation.per_shard to console so ops can watch.

perf-bot: perf/job-scheduled: kv-prefix-ttl-24h on dedicated-prod-3 (3 nodes) started at 1773500400

sara: One more note: kernel selection/batching earlier this week increased per-request KV updates (we now write slightly earlier to pre-warm cache) — that interacts with compaction pressure. Need to coordinate with eng-runtime on batching heuristics so we're not taxing the KV pager.

mike: I'll ping runtime team in eng-runtime and add a short sync to prioritize compaction-safe batching.

henry: For rollout I'd prefer canary on non-critical customers first. If metrics look good (mem down, frag down, p99 stable) we flip.

sara: Thanks all — I'll upload the full profile + replay harness to the thread in ~1h. Short term: patch to TTL sticky prefixes + opportunistic compaction seems low-risk and effective.

mike: :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Note: scheduled maintenance window 1773540000 for rolling kernel updates. Keep in mind for canaries.

sara: copying the perf job link: https://internal-ci/jobs/kv-prefix-ttl-24h
(added to the run queue)

mike: Great, keep updates in this thread.
